short_description.id: Kanayago adalah dewa pandai besi di wilayah Chūgoku Jepang, biasanya perempuan tetapi kadang laki-laki.
short_description.en: Kanayago is a deity of smiths in Japan’s Chūgoku region, usually female but sometimes male.

long_description.id: Kanayago adalah dewa pandai besi di wilayah Chūgoku Jepang, biasanya perempuan tetapi kadang laki-laki. Lukisan kuil menggambarkan dewa itu sebagai Sanbō Kōjin sinkretis.
long_description.en: Kanayago is a deity of smiths in Japan’s Chūgoku region, usually female but sometimes male. A shrine painting portrays the deity as syncretic Sanbō Kōjin.

long_description.id: Legenda kuil menyebut dewa itu tiba di Izumo dengan bangau putih. Kisah setempat menyebut dewa itu mengajarkan pandai besi.
long_description.en: A shrine legend has the deity reach Izumo on a white heron. Local accounts credit the deity with teaching smithing.

long_description.id: Menurut Tetsuzan hisho dari abad ke-18, Kanayago turun dari langit ke Provinsi Harima, lalu menunggang bangau putih mencari tempat tinggal hingga hinggap di pohon katsura di pegunungan. Setelah Abe Masashige membangun kuil untuknya, ia mengajarinya membuat besi dengan metode tatara; kuil itu kini berada di Hirose, Yasugi. Pada akhir abad ke-18 kepercayaan kepadanya sudah menyebar di antara para pembuat besi di wilayah Chūgoku.
long_description.en: According to the eighteenth-century Tetsuzan hisho, Kanayago descended from heaven to Harima Province, then rode a white heron in search of a home until she alighted on a katsura tree in the mountains. After Abe Masashige built her a shrine, she taught him to make iron by the tatara method; the shrine now stands in Hirose, Yasugi. By the late 1700s faith in her had spread among ironworkers of the Chūgoku region.

long_description.id: Ia sering digambarkan rewel, tidak puas dengan rupanya, dan cemburu pada perempuan lain, sehingga perempuan sering dilarang mendekati tungku saat peleburan. Kadang ia digambarkan menunggang rubah.
long_description.en: She is often described as finicky, unhappy with her looks and jealous of other women, so women were often forbidden to approach the furnace during smelting. She is sometimes shown riding a fox.

description.id: Ia cemburu pada perempuan lain, sehingga perempuan dilarang mendekati tungku.
description.en: She is jealous of other women, so women were kept away from the furnace.

short_description.id: Kāneikokala adalah dewa hiu pelindung dalam mitologi Hawaii yang dikenal menyelamatkan korban perahu karam; ikan kōkala diasosiasikan dengannya.
short_description.en: Kāneikokala is a protective shark god of Hawaiian mythology known for rescuing people from canoe wrecks; the kōkala fish is associated with him.

long_description.id: Menurut mitologi Hawaii, Kāneikokala menyelamatkan orang dari perahu karam, dan ikan kōkala diasosiasikan dengannya. Ia dihitung di antara hiu-hiu leluhur (mano kumupaʻa) terpenting, bersama Ku-hai-moana, Kane-huna-moku, Kau-huhu, dan Ka-moho-aliʻi, dan dikenal sebagai aumakua hiu yang baik hati yang membawa korban kapal karam dengan selamat ke pantai.
long_description.en: According to Hawaiian mythology, Kāneikokala rescued people from canoe wrecks, and the kōkala fish was associated with him. He is counted among the most important ancestral sharks (mano kumupaʻa), together with Ku-hai-moana, Kane-huna-moku, Kau-huhu and Ka-moho-aliʻi, and is known as a kindly shark aumakua who brings shipwrecked people safely to shore.

long_description.id: Sebuah tradisi Maui menceritakan bahwa Kāneikokala dan saudarinya mulanya manusia dan anggota kaum pendeta. Kāneikokala adalah kahuna yang mengampuni pelanggaran; setelah meninggal, keduanya menjadi ʻaumakua hiu pelindung yang membantu orang menolak kejahatan.
long_description.en: In one Maui tradition, Kāneikokala and his sister began as human beings who belonged to the priestly class. Kāneikokala was a kahuna who forgave transgressions; after death both became protective shark ʻaumakua who help people resist evil.

long_description.id: Samuel Kamakau mencatat bahwa bila kano pecah di laut, keturunan para pemujanya dapat memanggil Kāneikokala, yang kemudian muncul dan mengantar para penyintas ke pulau asal masing-masing. Ikan kōkala keramat baginya: orang Kahiki-nui takut memakannya, menyentuh makanan yang bersentuhan dengannya, atau bahkan melintasi asap tungku tempat ikan itu dimasak. Dewa-dewa hiu leluhur seperti dia juga dapat tampil sebagai burung hantu, ikan hilu, moʻo, atau manusia.
long_description.en: Samuel Kamakau wrote that when a canoe broke up at sea, descendants of his worshippers could summon Kāneikokala, who would appear and bring the survivors back to their home islands. The kōkala fish was sacred to him: the people of Kahiki-nui feared to eat it, to touch food that had touched it, or even to cross the smoke of an oven where it was cooking. Ancestral shark gods like him could also appear as owls, hilu fish, moʻo or humans.

long_description.id: Sebuah batu yang dipuja sebagai Kāneikokala pernah disembunyikan untuk melindunginya ketika arca dewa-dewa Hawaii terancam. Sekitar 1885 seorang lelaki tua bernama Wahinenui bermimpi Kāneikokala mengeluh kedinginan dan minta digali. Batu itu sampai di Bishop Museum pada 1906 dan dipasang di lantai Hawaiian Hall; ketika hendak dipindahkan, pekerja gagal mencapai dasarnya sampai para tetua mengingatkan bahwa Kāneikokala tidak dimintai izin, sehingga batu itu tetap di tempatnya.
long_description.en: A stone revered as Kāneikokala was once buried for safety during a period when Hawaiian god images were under threat. In about 1885 an old man named Wahinenui dreamed that Kāneikokala complained of the cold and asked to be dug up. The stone came to the Bishop Museum in 1906 and was set into the floor of Hawaiian Hall; when staff tried to move it, workers could not reach its base until elders pointed out that Kāneikokala had not been consulted, and the stone stayed where it was.

short_description.id: Karajishi adalah sosok singa suci bergaya dalam seni Jepang dengan pengaruh Tiongkok.
short_description.en: Karajishi are stylized sacred lion figures of Japanese art with Chinese influence.

long_description.id: Karajishi adalah sosok singa suci bergaya dalam seni Jepang dengan pengaruh Tiongkok. Mereka memiliki surai keriting, mata menonjol, kaki kuat, serta cakar atau taring berlebihan.
long_description.en: Karajishi are stylized sacred lion figures of Japanese art with Chinese influence. They have curled manes, prominent eyes, strong legs and exaggerated claws or fangs.

long_description.id: Motif peoni umum, sedangkan konsep artistiknya dibedakan dari komainu dan shīsā. Kaitan Buddha menghubungkan singa dengan Shakyamuni, Monju, serta citra penjaga suci.
long_description.en: Peony motifs are common, while the artistic concept is distinguished from komainu and shīsā. Buddhist associations connect lions with Shakyamuni, Monju and sacred guardian imagery.

long_description.id: Sebagai kata, karajishi berarti "binatang asing", untuk membedakan singa dari babi hutan dan rusa yang hidup di Jepang. Dalam seni, singa yang distilisasi ini terutama populer sejak zaman Momoyama dan banyak dilukis pada layar lipat, sekat, dan pintu geser fusuma. Karajishi juga menjadi nama lambang keluarga berbentuk singa, yang tercatat pada tahun 1687.
long_description.en: As a word, karajishi means "foreign beast", distinguishing the lion from the wild boar and deer of Japan. In art, this stylised lion became especially popular from the Momoyama period and was often painted on folding screens, partitions and fusuma sliding doors. Karajishi is also the name of a lion-shaped family crest, attested in 1687.

short_description.id: Keneō adalah oni tua di tepi Sungai Sanzu dalam dunia bawah Buddha yang menggantung pakaian arwah pada pohon untuk menimbang dosa mereka.
short_description.en: Keneō is an old oni on the bank of the Sanzu River in the Buddhist underworld who hangs the souls' clothing on a tree to weigh their sins.

long_description.id: Keneō adalah oni yang duduk di tepi Sungai Sanzu dalam dunia bawah Buddha. Namanya berarti kakek penggantung pakaian. Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, ia dikatakan berada di atas pohon Eryōju atau di samping Datsueba di tepi sungai, dan, bersama Datsueba, berada di bawah Sepuluh Raja.
long_description.en: Keneō is an oni stationed on the bank of the Sanzu River in the Buddhist underworld. His name means "old man who hangs clothes". According to Japanese Wikipedia he is said to be on the Eryōju tree or beside Datsueba on the riverbank, and, together with Datsueba, he serves under the Ten Kings.

long_description.id: Dalam tradisi Jepang, enam mon diletakkan bersama jenazah sebagai bayaran untuk masuk ke dunia bawah. Ketika arwah tiba di sungai, Datsue-ba memaksa mereka melepas pakaian, dan Keneō menggantungnya pada dahan di tepi sungai yang melengkung sesuai berat dosa. Bila arwah datang tanpa pakaian, Keneō menguliti orang itu dan menggantung kulitnya.
long_description.en: In Japanese tradition six mon are placed with the body as payment to enter the underworld. When souls arrive at the river, Datsue-ba forces them to take off their clothes and Keneō hangs these on a riverside branch that bends according to the weight of their sins. A soul that has no clothes at all has its skin stripped off by Keneō, who hangs that on the tree instead.

long_description.id: Yokai.com menambahkan bahwa Datsueba dan Keneō juga menyiksa sendiri, misalnya mematahkan jari para pencuri, dan berkeliling di tepi sungai menyiksa arwah anak-anak yang terlalu muda untuk menyeberang. Sebuah ensiklopedia mencatat bahwa ajaran tentang Sungai Sanzu bukan ajaran Buddha, melainkan kepercayaan populer.
long_description.en: Yokai.com adds that Datsueba and Keneō also carry out some torture themselves, such as breaking the fingers of thieves, and roam the bank tormenting the souls of children too young to cross the river. An encyclopedia notes that the Sanzu River is not Buddhist doctrine but folk belief.

short_description.id: Kidōmaru adalah oni dalam Kokon Chomonjū zaman Kamakura, dikenal karena bersembunyi di dalam sapi mati untuk menyergap Minamoto no Yorimitsu.
short_description.en: Kidōmaru is an oni in the Kamakura-period Kokon Chomonjū, known for hiding inside a dead cow to ambush Minamoto no Yorimitsu.

long_description.id: Kidōmaru (鬼童丸, 鬼同丸) adalah oni yang muncul dalam Kokon Chomonjū, kumpulan setsuwa zaman Kamakura, dan beberapa sumber lain. Dalam teks itu, Minamoto no Yorimitsu, yang dikenal karena membunuh Shuten-dōji, mengunjungi rumah adiknya, Minamoto no Yorinobu, dan melihat Kidōmaru diikat. Yorimitsu menyarankan agar ia diikat dengan rantai, tetapi Kidōmaru mudah memutus rantai itu dan, menyimpan dendam, mengawasi tempat tidur Yorimitsu.
long_description.en: Kidōmaru (鬼童丸, 鬼同丸) is an oni appearing in the Kokon Chomonjū, a Kamakura-period collection of setsuwa, and in other sources. In that text Minamoto no Yorimitsu, known for slaying Shuten-dōji, visits the home of his brother Minamoto no Yorinobu and sees Kidōmaru held captive. Yorimitsu advises restraining him with chains, but Kidōmaru easily tears them off and, bearing a grudge, keeps watch over Yorimitsu's bed.

long_description.id: Yorimitsu mengatakan akan berkunjung ke kuil Kurama keesokan harinya. Kidōmaru mendahului ke Kurama, membunuh seekor sapi lepasan di ladang Ichihara, bersembunyi di dalam tubuhnya, dan menunggu. Ketika sebuah panah menembus sapi itu, Kidōmaru muncul dengan pedang dan menyerang Yorimitsu, tetapi Yorimitsu menebasnya dengan satu tebasan. Teks itu menambahkan bahwa ia tetap garang sampai mati.
long_description.en: Yorimitsu said he would visit the Kurama temple the next day. Kidōmaru went ahead to Kurama, killed a free-ranging cow at the Ichihara field, hid inside its body, and waited. When an arrow was shot through the cow, Kidōmaru appeared with a sword and attacked Yorimitsu, but Yorimitsu struck him down with a single strike. The text adds that he stayed fierce until his death.

long_description.id: Sumber lain memberi latar yang berbeda. Zentaiheiki menyebut oni ini semula anak kecil di Gunung Hiei yang diusir karena perbuatan jahat lalu menjadi bandit di sebuah gua, sedangkan tradisi lisan Kumohara di Fukuchiyama menyebutnya anak Shuten-dōji. Catatan pameran Ritsumeikan menyebutnya sebagai anak asuh di Gunung Hiei yang mempelajari ilmu sihir jalan tengu dan tinggal di gua di Ichihara-no. Toriyama Sekien menggambarkannya dengan judul "Kidō" mengenakan kulit sapi di tengah salju.
long_description.en: Other sources give different backgrounds. The Zentaiheiki says this oni was originally a young child on Mount Hiei who was chased away for wicked deeds and became a bandit in a cave, while the oral tradition of Kumohara in Fukuchiyama calls him a child of Shuten-dōji. The Ritsumeikan exhibition note describes an acolyte on Mount Hiei who learned the sorcery of the tengu path and lived in a cave in Ichihara field. Toriyama Sekien depicted him, under the title "Kidō", wearing a cow's skin in the snow.

claims.quote: Kidōmaru (鬼童丸, 鬼同丸) is an oni that appears in the Kamakura period collection of setsuwa, the Kokon Chomonjū, among other sources.

statement.id: Kidōmaru adalah oni dalam Kokon Chomonjū dari zaman Kamakura.
statement.en: Kidōmaru is an oni in the Kamakura-period Kokon Chomonjū.

claims.quote: Yorimitsu said that Yorinobu was careless, so they should restrain the oni with chains, and stayed at Yorinobu's house for that night.

statement.id: Satu cerita menyebut Yorimitsu memerintahkan agar ia diikat dengan rantai.
statement.en: A tale has Yorimitsu order him restrained with chains.

claims.quote: Kidōmaru easily tore off those chains, and with a grudge against Yorimitsu, looked at his bed and kept watch.

statement.id: Ia memutus rantai dan menyimpan dendam terhadap Yorimitsu.
statement.en: He breaks the chains and bears a grudge against Yorimitsu.

claims.quote: Yorimitsu noticed this and told a servant, "tomorrow, I will make a visit to the Kurama temple." Kidōmaru then went ahead to Kurama, killed one free-ranging cattle at the Ichihara field, hid inside its body, and waited for Yorimitsu to come.

statement.id: Ia bersembunyi di dalam sapi yang dibunuh sambil menunggu untuk menyergap Yorimitsu.
statement.en: He hides inside a slain cow while waiting to ambush Yorimitsu.

claims.quote: It is said that Kidōmaru appeared from inside the cow and tried to slash at Yorimitsu, but Yorimitsu struck down Kidōmaru with a single strike.

statement.id: Pertemuan itu berakhir dengan Yorimitsu membunuhnya.
statement.en: The encounter ends with Yorimitsu killing him.

claims.quote: In the yōkai pictures collection, the Konjaku Hyakki Shūi by Toriyama Sekien, under the title of "Kidō," it depicts Kidōmaru in the snow wearing the skin of a cattle waiting for Yorimitsu to come.

statement.id: Sekien menggambarnya memakai kulit sapi di tengah salju.
statement.en: Sekien depicts him wearing a cow’s hide in the snow.

claims.quote: According to the oral traditions of Kumohara in Fukuchiyama, Kyoto Prefecture, there is the following legend about Kidōmaru as a child of Shuten-dōji.

statement.id: Menurut tradisi lisan Kumohara di Fukuchiyama, Prefektur Kyoto, ada legenda tentang Kidōmaru sebagai anak Shuten-dōji.
statement.en: According to the oral traditions of Kumohara in Fukuchiyama, Kyoto Prefecture, there is a legend about Kidōmaru as a child of Shuten-dōji.

claims.quote: The Zentaiheiki, a collection of war tales, theorizes this oni to instead be an abandoned child of Shuten-dōji, and originally Kidōmaru was a young child at Mount Hiei but came to ruin as a result of wicked deeds, and was therefore chased away from Mount Hiei, and then migrated to a cave in the mountains and became a bandit.

statement.id: Zentaiheiki, kumpulan kisah perang, berteori bahwa oni ini adalah anak terbuang Shuten-dōji yang semula anak kecil di Gunung Hiei, jatuh karena perbuatan jahat, diusir dari Gunung Hiei, lalu pindah ke gua di pegunungan dan menjadi bandit.
statement.en: The Zentaiheiki, a collection of war tales, theorizes that this oni was an abandoned child of Shuten-dōji who was originally a young child at Mount Hiei, came to ruin through wicked deeds, was chased away from Mount Hiei, and then moved to a cave in the mountains and became a bandit.

claims.quote: According to the "Shitennō Shōtō Iroku" (四天王剿盗異録) by Takizawa Bakin, at a cave in the mountains, Kidōmaru met Hakamadare, a bandit of the Konjaku Monogatarishū, where there was a scene of a contest comparing skills.

statement.id: Menurut Shitennō Shōtō Iroku karya Takizawa Bakin, Kidōmaru bertemu Hakamadare, bandit dari Konjaku Monogatarishū, di sebuah gua di pegunungan, tempat terjadi adegan adu kemampuan.
statement.en: According to the Shitennō Shōtō Iroku by Takizawa Bakin, Kidōmaru met Hakamadare, a bandit of the Konjaku Monogatarishū, at a cave in the mountains, where there was a scene of a contest comparing skills.

claims.quote: 盃酌(はいしやく)の間、頼光、厩(うまや)の方を見やりたりければ、童を一人いましめて置きたりけり。

statement.id: Dalam teks Kokon Chomonjū, saat minum-minum, Raikō memandang ke arah kandang kuda dan melihat seorang anak lelaki diikat di sana.
statement.en: In the Kokon Chomonjū text, while drinking, Raikō looked toward the stable and saw a boy kept bound there.

claims.quote: 夜の中、静まるほどに、鬼同丸、究竟(くつくやう)の者にて、いましめたる縄・金鏁踏み切りて、逃れ出でぬ。

statement.id: Dalam teks Kokon Chomonjū, ketika malam telah sunyi, Kidōmaru, sosok yang tangguh, memutus tali dan rantai logam pengikatnya lalu kabur.
statement.en: In the Kokon Chomonjū text, when the night had grown quiet, Kidōmaru, a formidable fellow, broke the bonding rope and metal chain and escaped.

claims.quote: 野飼ひの牛のあまたありける中に、ことに大きなるを殺して、路頭に引き伏せて、牛の腹をかき破りて、その中に入りて、目ばかり見出だして侍りけり。

statement.id: Di antara banyak sapi lepasan, ia membunuh yang paling besar, membaringkannya di jalan, merobek perutnya, lalu masuk ke dalamnya dengan hanya matanya yang terlihat.
statement.en: Among many free-grazing cattle, he killed an especially large one, laid it on the road, tore open its belly, and entered it, showing only his eyes.

claims.quote: 牛の腹のほどを指して矢を放ちたるに、死にたる牛、ゆすゆすとはたらきて、腹の内より大の童、打刀(うちがたな)を抜きて、走り出でて、頼光にかかりけり。見れば鬼同丸なりけり。

statement.id: Ketika sebatang panah dilepaskan ke perut sapi mati itu, sapi itu bergerak, dan dari dalamnya berlari keluar seorang anak besar dengan pedang terhunus menyerang Raikō; ia adalah Kidōmaru.
statement.en: When an arrow was shot at the belly of the dead cow, it stirred, and from inside a large boy ran out with a drawn sword and attacked Raikō; it was Kidōmaru.

claims.quote: 頼光も少しも騒がで、太刀を抜きて、鬼同丸が頸(くび)を打ち落してけり。

statement.id: Raikō sama sekali tidak panik, menghunus pedang, dan memenggal kepala Kidōmaru.
statement.en: Raikō, not at all alarmed, drew his sword and struck off Kidōmaru's head.

claims.quote: 死ぬるまで武(たけ)くいかめしう侍りけるよし、語り伝へたり。

statement.id: Diceritakan turun-temurun bahwa ia tetap garang dan menakutkan sampai mati.
statement.en: It is handed down that he remained fierce and formidable until he died.

claims.quote: 保昌と直接関わるのではないが、頼光説話の中で、酒呑童子退治の後日譚として伝わるのが、鬼童丸（鬼同丸とも）である。

statement.id: Catatan pameran Ritsumeikan menyebut bahwa dalam kisah Raikō, Kidōmaru (juga ditulis 鬼同丸) diwariskan sebagai kelanjutan kisah penumpasan Shuten-dōji.
statement.en: The Ritsumeikan exhibition note says that, within the Raikō tales, Kidōmaru (also written 鬼同丸) is transmitted as a sequel to the slaying of Shuten-dōji.

claims.quote: 鬼童丸は、比叡山にあって大師坊の稚児であったが、力は人に優れ、稚児法師を殺し、経論を焼き捨て、天狗道の妖術も学んで仏法を破滅させようとして、山を追出された。

statement.id: Kidōmaru adalah anak asuh (chigo) Daishi-bō di Gunung Hiei yang kekuatannya melebihi manusia; ia membunuh seorang chigo-hōshi, membakar kitab suci, mempelajari ilmu sihir jalan tengu, berusaha menghancurkan ajaran Buddha, dan diusir dari gunung.
statement.en: Kidōmaru was an acolyte of the Daishi-bō on Mount Hiei, superior in strength to others; he killed an acolyte monk, burned scriptures, learned the sorcery of the tengu path, tried to destroy Buddhism, and was driven off the mountain.

claims.quote: 市原野の洞窟に住み、天狗等と語らい、世間を悩ませていたが、頼光の弟の源頼信とその郎党により生け捕りにされた。

statement.id: Ia tinggal di gua di Ichihara-no, bergaul dengan tengu dan meresahkan masyarakat, sampai ditangkap hidup-hidup oleh Minamoto no Yorinobu, adik Raikō, dan para pengikutnya.
statement.en: He lived in a cave in Ichihara field, conversed with tengu, and troubled the world until he was captured alive by Raikō's brother Minamoto no Yorinobu and his retainers.

claims.quote: 鬼童丸は、天狗との結託、比叡山からの追放により、人間でありながら異界に一歩踏出した異人である。

statement.id: Catatan itu menafsirkan Kidōmaru, karena persekongkolannya dengan tengu dan pengusirannya dari Gunung Hiei, sebagai orang asing yang meski manusia telah melangkah satu langkah ke dunia lain.
statement.en: The note interprets Kidōmaru, through his collusion with tengu and expulsion from Mount Hiei, as an outsider who, though human, had taken a step into the other world.

summary.id: Kokon Chomonjū (seperti dikutip sumber pertama): oni yang menyimpan dendam pada Yorimitsu.
summary.en: Kokon Chomonjū (as cited by the first source): an oni bearing a grudge against Yorimitsu.

summary.id: Tradisi lisan Kumohara: anak Shuten-dōji.
summary.en: Kumohara oral tradition: a child of Shuten-dōji.

summary.id: Zentaiheiki: anak kecil di Gunung Hiei yang diusir lalu menjadi bandit.
summary.en: Zentaiheiki: a young child at Mount Hiei who was chased away and became a bandit.

summary.id: Catatan Ritsumeikan: manusia yang telah melangkah ke dunia lain.
summary.en: Ritsumeikan note: a human who had stepped into the other world.

short_description.id: Kimpurusha adalah kelompok makhluk dalam sastra Hindu yang memiliki tubuh manusia dan kepala singa.
short_description.en: Kimpurushas are beings in Hindu literature described as human-bodied with lion heads.

long_description.id: Kimpurusha adalah kelompok makhluk dalam sastra Hindu yang memiliki tubuh manusia dan kepala singa. Mereka dikaitkan dengan kinnara, tetapi beberapa Purana membedakan keduanya.
long_description.en: Kimpurushas are beings in Hindu literature described as human-bodied with lion heads. They are associated with kinnaras, but some Puranas distinguish the two.

long_description.id: Mereka merupakan pelayan Kubera, dewa kekayaan. Brahma dikatakan menciptakan kimpurusha dan kinnara dari pantulan dirinya. Mereka memuji Narasimha setelah ia membunuh Hiranyakashipu. Budha mengubah sejumlah perempuan menjadi kimpurushi dan menyuruh mereka tinggal di gunung.
long_description.en: They serve Kubera, the wealth god. Brahma is said to create kimpurushas and kinnaras from his reflected image. They praise Narasimha after he kills Hiranyakashipu. Budha changes women into kimpurushis and instructs them to dwell on a mountain.

long_description.id: Dalam salah satu rujukan ringkasan, kimpurusa disebut sebagai putra Pulaha Prajapati dan beribu perempuan yaksa. Mereka menjaga kolam teratai milik Kubera. Dalam tradisi Jain, kimpurusa adalah golongan dewa kinnara yang semuanya berwarna keemasan menurut Tiloyapannatti.
long_description.en: In one reference summary, the kimpurushas are called sons of Pulaha Prajapati with Yaksha women as their mothers. They guard the lotus ponds kept by Kubera. In Jain tradition, the kimpurushas are a class of kinnara deities, all golden in appearance according to the Tiloyapannatti.

description.id: Dalam kedua tradisi Jain, kimpurusa adalah golongan dewa kinnara, dan semuanya berwarna keemasan menurut Tiloyapannatti.
description.en: In both Jain traditions, kimpurushas are a class of kinnara deities, and all are golden in appearance according to the Tiloyapannatti.

role.en: Guardians of Kubera's lotus ponds.

claims.quote: The kimpurushas (Sanskrit: किंपुरुष, romanized: Kimpuruṣa) are a race of beings featured in Hindu literature, described as possessing the bodies of human beings and lion heads. They are associated with, and sometimes considered the same as the kinnaras, though some Puranas distinguish between them. They are attendants of the god of wealth, Kubera.

statement.id: Kimpurusha adalah kelompok makhluk dalam sastra Hindu yang memiliki tubuh manusia dan kepala singa.

claims.quote: They are associated with, and sometimes considered the same as the kinnaras, though some Puranas distinguish between them.

statement.id: Mereka dikaitkan dengan kinnara, tetapi beberapa Purana membedakan keduanya.

claims.quote: They are attendants of the god of wealth, Kubera.

claims.quote: The kimpurushas, along with a number of other beings, praise the glory of the Narasimha avatar of Vishnu after he slays Hiranyakashipu.

statement.id: Mereka memuji Narasimha setelah ia membunuh Hiranyakashipu.
statement.en: They praise Narasimha after he kills Hiranyakashipu.

claims.quote: Budha transforms a number of women into kimpurushis (female kimpurushas) and instructs them to make a mountain their abode and take kimpurushas for their consorts.

short_description.id: Kodinhaltija adalah roh penjaga rumah dalam tradisi rakyat yang tinggal dekat perapian dan diberi bagian makanan agar tidak mengganggu.
short_description.en: The kodinhaltija is a house guardian spirit of folk tradition that lives by the hearth and is given a share of food so it will not cause trouble.

long_description.id: Dalam tradisi rakyat, kodinhaltija atau kotitonttu adalah haltija atau tonttu yang dipercaya tinggal di rumah hunian. Ia sering dipercaya datang saat api pertama kali dinyalakan di rumah; kadang yang menjadi kodinhaltija adalah orang pertama yang menyalakan api, biasanya pendiri rumah, atau orang pertama yang meninggal di sana. Ia biasanya berdiam di dekat perapian dan kadang membanting pintu tungku sebagai tanda kedatangan tamu.
long_description.en: In folk tradition the kodinhaltija or kotitonttu is a haltija or tonttu believed to live in the house. It was often thought to arrive when a fire was first lit there; sometimes the first fire-maker, often the founder, or the first person to die in the house became the kodinhaltija. It usually stays by the hearth and sometimes bangs the stove door to announce a visitor.

long_description.id: Di meja makan ia sering diberi bagiannya lebih dulu, karena kodinhaltija yang diperlakukan buruk akan mengganggu, dan penampakannya dianggap pertanda kecelakaan atau kematian. Saat rumah baru dibangun, batu perapian, abu, atau tanah dari rumah lama dibawa agar ia ikut pindah.
long_description.en: At meals it was often served first, since a badly treated kodinhaltija would cause trouble, and its appearance was taken as an omen of misfortune or death. When a new house was built, stones, ash or soil from the old hearth were brought along so that it would move too.

long_description.id: Holmberg mencatat bahwa bangsa Finn Baltik menyebut roh rumah "Sang Penguasa" (Haltia; dalam bahasa Estonia Haldja). Orang harus memohon izin kepadanya saat menempati rumah baru, bahkan saat menginap semalam. Bila satu batang kayu rumah lama dipakai lagi, Haltia ikut pindah ke rumah baru, dan abu semua perapian dibawa ke perapian baru.
long_description.en: Holmberg notes that the Baltic Finns call the household spirit "the Ruler" (Haltia; Esthonian Haldja). People had to ask its permission when settling in a new dwelling, even when staying anywhere for a night. If one log of the old house was used again, the Haltia moved with it into the new house, and the ashes of all the hearths were taken to the new fireplaces.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan yang umum di Finlandia, orang yang pertama meninggal di rumah atau yang pertama menyalakan api di sana menjadi Haltia rumah itu. Haltia laki-laki berkedudukan lebih tinggi daripada yang perempuan, tetapi anak-anak tumbuh lebih baik bila Haltia-nya perempuan. Di Ingria, Haltia konon menampakkan diri sebagai anjing atau kucing belang sebagai pertanda kebakaran.
long_description.en: A widespread Finnish belief held that whoever was the first to die in a house, or to light its first fire, became that house's Haltia. The male Haltia ranked above the female, but children grew up better where the Haltia was a woman. In Ingria the Haltia is said to have appeared as a dog or a mottled or striped cat as a sign of fire.

short_description.id: Komat adalah salah satu dari dua saudara kembar pencipta dunia dalam tradisi suku Cucapá di utara Meksiko.
short_description.en: Komat is one of the twin creator brothers in the tradition of the Cucapá of northern Mexico.

long_description.id: Dalam tradisi Cucapá, Komat dan saudara kembarnya Sipa hidup di bawah air dekat pusat bumi. Komat membantu Sipa naik ke permukaan, lalu bertanya apakah aman keluar dengan mata terbuka; Sipa berkata ya, dan Komat menjadi buta.
long_description.en: In Cucapá tradition Komat and his twin Sipa lived beneath the water near the centre of the earth. Komat helped Sipa reach the surface and asked whether it was safe to come out with open eyes; Sipa said yes, and Komat was blinded.

long_description.id: Keduanya meminta semut merah bersayap menggali bumi agar air surut, lalu membentuk boneka tanah liat yang menjadi manusia. Seperti dalam banyak mitos penciptaan, keduanya melambangkan dualitas baik dan jahat.
long_description.en: They asked flying red ants to dig the earth so the waters receded, then shaped clay figures that became people. As in many creation myths, the pair represent the duality of good and evil.

long_description.id: Sebuah artikel surat kabar regional menuturkan versi yang berbeda: Sipa dan Komat muncul dari laut purba, Komat keluar lebih dulu dengan mata tertutup, sedangkan yang membuka mata di dalam air lalu menjadi buta adalah Sipa. Semut membantu mereka membawa tanah dari kedalaman untuk membentuk daratan, dan bersama-sama mereka menciptakan berbagai bangsa. Namun persaingan mereka memuncak ketika Komat turun ke dunia bawah dan melepaskan penyakit serta kematian ke dunia.
long_description.en: A regional newspaper article gives a different version: Sipa and Komat emerged from a primordial sea, Komat came out first with his eyes closed, and it was Sipa who opened his eyes underwater and was blinded. Ants helped them bring earth from the depths to form the land, and together they created various peoples. But their rivalry climaxed when Komat descended into the underworld, releasing sickness and death into the world.

short_description.id: Konaki-jiji adalah yōkai yang dikaitkan dengan pegunungan Tokushima, berwujud lelaki tua atau bayi yang menangis lalu menjadi sangat berat setelah digendong.
short_description.en: Konaki-jiji is a yōkai associated with the mountains of Tokushima, an old man or baby that cries and becomes very heavy once picked up.

long_description.id: Konaki-jiji adalah yōkai yang dikaitkan dengan daerah pegunungan Prefektur Tokushima. Namanya biasa diterjemahkan sebagai kakek yang menangis seperti bayi. Folklorist Yanagita Kunio mencatatnya sebagai yōkai berwujud lelaki tua yang menangis seperti bayi baru lahir di jalan malam.
long_description.en: Konaki-jiji is a yōkai associated with the mountain regions of Tokushima Prefecture. Its name is usually translated as an old man crying like a baby. The folklorist Yanagita Kunio recorded it as a yōkai in the form of an old man who cries like a newborn on night roads.

long_description.id: Menurut ceritanya, yōkai ini dapat tampak sebagai lelaki tua atau bayi dan memancing pejalan agar mengangkatnya. Setelah diangkat, ia menjadi sangat berat dan menindih korban. Yokai.com menggambarkannya membawa tongkat jalan dan mengenakan jas hujan jerami di atas pakaian bayi yang kebesaran.
long_description.en: In the stories this yōkai can appear as an old man or a baby and lures a traveler into picking it up. Once picked up, it becomes extremely heavy and crushes the victim. Yokai.com describes it carrying a walking stick and wearing a straw raincoat over oversized baby clothes.

long_description.id: Keaslian tradisinya diperdebatkan. Yanagita menunjuk ciri-cirinya sebagai rekaan yang dekat dengan obariyon dan ubume, dan sejarawan lokal Takita Masahiro menemukan bahwa legendanya sebenarnya tidak ada di Tokushima. Yokai.com menyebut ia diduga tercipta dari penggabungan dua cerita rakyat. Sejak tampil dalam GeGeGe no Kitarō karya Mizuki Shigeru ia terkenal sebagai yōkai yang membantu Kitarō.
long_description.en: The authenticity of the tradition is debated. Yanagita pointed to its features as an invention close to the obariyon and the ubume, and the local historian Takita Masahiro found that the legend does not actually exist in Tokushima. Yokai.com says it is thought to have been created by combining two folktales. Since appearing in Mizuki Shigeru's GeGeGe no Kitarō it has been famous as a yōkai that helps Kitarō.

claims.quote: Konaki-jiji (子泣き爺; also romanized konaki-jijii or konakijijii) is a yōkai — a supernatural creature from Japanese folklore — originating in the mountain regions of Tokushima Prefecture on the island of Shikoku.

statement.en: Konaki-jiji is a yōkai associated with the mountains of Tokushima.

claims.quote: The konaki-jiji is notable for its deceptive method of attack: it lures compassionate travelers by mimicking the sound of an infant crying in the wilderness, then, once picked up, becomes supernaturally heavy, crushing its victim to death.

statement.id: Konaki-jiji adalah salah satu yōkai yang dicatat dalam buku Yōkai Dangi karya folklorist Yanagita Kunio; pada dasarnya berwujud lelaki tua yang dikatakan menangis seperti bayi di jalan malam.
statement.en: Konaki-jiji is one of the yōkai described in the folklorist Yanagita Kunio's Yōkai Dangi; it is originally an old man said to cry like a newborn on night roads.

claims.quote: しかし、柳田はこうした特徴について、おばりよんや産女に近いものとして、創作と指摘している。

statement.id: Yanagita menilai ciri-ciri itu mirip obariyon dan ubume, dan menunjuknya sebagai rekaan.
statement.en: Yanagita regarded these features as close to those of the obariyon and the ubume, and pointed to them as an invention.

claims.quote: 阿南市の郷土史家の多喜田昌裕によれば、伝承地とされる徳島県地方では、実際には子泣き爺の伝説は存在しないことが判明している。

statement.id: Menurut sejarawan lokal Anan, Takita Masahiro, legenda Konaki-jiji ternyata tidak benar-benar ada di wilayah Prefektur Tokushima yang disebut sebagai tempat asalnya.
statement.en: According to the Anan local historian Takita Masahiro, it has been found that no Konaki-jiji legend actually exists in the Tokushima region said to be its home.

claims.quote: 2001年には多喜田と地元の有志団により、徳島県三好郡山城町（現・三好市）が伝承の発祥地と認定され、現地には「児啼爺」の名の石像と、京極夏彦による「児啼爺の碑」が建てられ、同年に山城町にて除幕式が行われた。

statement.id: Pada 2001, Takita dan sukarelawan setempat menetapkan Yamashiro-chō (kini Miyoshi), Tokushima, sebagai tempat asal legendanya; dibangun patung batu bernama "児啼爺" dan prasasti oleh Kyōgoku Natsuhiko.
statement.en: In 2001 Takita and local volunteers certified Yamashiro-chō (now Miyoshi), Tokushima, as the legend's birthplace; a stone statue named "児啼爺" and a monument by Kyōgoku Natsuhiko were erected there.

claims.quote: 特に水木しげるの漫画・アニメ『ゲゲゲの鬼太郎』で主人公の鬼太郎をサポートする名脇役として描かれて以降は、正義の妖怪として一躍有名な存在となっている。

statement.id: Sejak digambarkan dalam manga dan anime GeGeGe no Kitarō karya Mizuki Shigeru sebagai tokoh pendukung yang membantu Kitarō, ia mendadak terkenal sebagai yōkai yang berpihak pada kebenaran.
statement.en: Since Mizuki Shigeru's manga and anime GeGeGe no Kitarō portrayed it as a fine supporting character helping the hero Kitarō, it has become suddenly famous as a yōkai on the side of justice.

claims.quote: Konaki jijii are mountain-dwelling spirits who look like old human men. They carry walking sticks and wear straw raincoats on top of over-sized baby clothes.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, konaki jijii adalah roh penghuni gunung yang tampak seperti lelaki tua, membawa tongkat jalan dan memakai jas hujan jerami di atas pakaian bayi berukuran kebesaran.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, konaki jijii are mountain-dwelling spirits that look like old men, carrying walking sticks and wearing straw raincoats over oversized baby clothes.

claims.quote: When they hug the crying spirit, it rapidly becomes heavier and heavier. The konaki jijii clings to its victim, who is unable to pull themself free.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, bila orang memeluk roh yang menangis itu, ia dengan cepat menjadi makin berat dan menempel pada korban yang tidak bisa melepaskan diri.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, when someone hugs the crying spirit it rapidly grows heavier and clings to the victim, who cannot pull free.

claims.quote: It is thought to be a yōkai that was invented by combining two different folktales into a new form.

statement.id: Yokai.com menyebut ia diduga yōkai yang tercipta dari penggabungan dua cerita rakyat yang berbeda.
statement.en: Yokai.com says it is thought to be a yōkai invented by combining two different folktales.

claims.quote: This pattern of behavior—tricking passersby into helping a crying baby and then crushing them like a stone—is shared by several yōkai across Japan, such as obariyon, ubume, and nure onna.

statement.id: Yokai.com menyebut pola menipu orang agar menolong bayi yang menangis lalu menindihnya serupa dengan beberapa yōkai lain di Jepang, seperti obariyon, ubume, dan nure onna.
statement.en: Yokai.com says the pattern of tricking passersby into helping a crying baby and then crushing them is shared by several other yōkai across Japan, such as obariyon, ubume and nure onna.

claims.quote: 子泣き爺と同様、赤ん坊のような産声をあげるという「ごぎゃ泣き（ごぎゃなき）」という妖怪が四国に伝わっている。

statement.id: Di Shikoku diwariskan yōkai "gogyanaki" yang, seperti Konaki-jiji, dikatakan menangis seperti bayi baru lahir.
statement.en: In Shikoku a yōkai called "gogyanaki" is handed down which, like Konaki-jiji, is said to cry like a newborn baby.

topic.id: Apakah legenda Konaki-jiji benar-benar berasal dari Tokushima
topic.en: Whether the Konaki-jiji legend really originates in Tokushima

summary.id: Satu artikel ensiklopedia daring: berasal dari daerah pegunungan Prefektur Tokushima di Pulau Shikoku.
summary.en: One online-encyclopedia article: it originates in the mountain regions of Tokushima Prefecture on the island of Shikoku.

summary.id: Artikel berbahasa Jepang: sejarawan lokal Takita Masahiro menyatakan legenda Konaki-jiji sebenarnya tidak ada di Tokushima; Yanagita menilai ciri-cirinya rekaan.
summary.en: Japanese-language article: the local historian Takita Masahiro states no Konaki-jiji legend actually exists in Tokushima; Yanagita judged its features to be an invention.

gaps.searched: Belum ada berkas Wikimedia Commons yang diverifikasi untuk entri ini; tidak dicari ulang pada putaran ini.
Dibuka: Wikipedia bahasa Inggris dan Jepang, yokai.com (Matthew Meyer), kotobank.jp (tidak ada entri untuk 子泣き爺 maupun 児啼爺). Teks Yōkai Dangi karya Yanagita tidak ditemukan terbuka secara daring.

selection_criteria: computeFillStatus must be lengkap-informasi: complete, valid research without an approved image.
No active editorial artwork and no permanent artwork exclusion.
The accepted research entry is embedded unchanged; the image may only depict what its claims document.
Creatures an earlier batch left out keep that reason as catatan_sebelumnya; the generator may decline them with status tidak-digambar.

user_policy.name: sangar
user_policy.intent: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.
user_policy.subject: The being dominates the frame and is clearly the subject. Head, eyes and distinguishing traits are readable even at thumbnail size. Never a landscape without the being, never a human who could be a passer-by, never a farm animal at pasture.
user_policy.moment: Depict a moment, not a pose: hunting, emerging, striking, commanding, towering, descending, tearing through weather or ground. Gaze and posture confront or loom over the viewer. Standing still and facing the camera with a neutral expression is not acceptable.
user_policy.effects: Visible power is wanted and may be strong, but every effect must come from a power, domain, attribute, habitat or deed documented in the research claims of that being, and it must act physically on the world: ground cracking, water rearing, trees bending, lightning striking, flame consuming, fog pouring, bodies of victims turned to stone. No generic glowing envelope, neon outline, energy ribbons, floating runes or luminous coloured mist. If the research documents no power, build menace from anatomy, scale, moment, light and setting instead, and record that in artistic_choices.
user_policy.fidelity: Anatomy, attributes, number of heads, eyes, limbs and iconography follow the research claims exactly. Effects and atmosphere add power; they never replace or invent anatomy. Fully opaque clothing where a humanlike form is clothed; no nudity, no explicit gore.
user_policy.composition: Low camera angle; monumental or predatory scale with small environmental references when size is documented, otherwise dominance through tight framing and foreshortening. Strong silhouette, high contrast, cinematic low-key lighting from one dominant source (moon, fire, lightning, dying sun), rim light, dust, smoke, rain or spray. Tactile surfaces: wet scales, matted fur, cracked skin, rust, weathered cloth, stone.
user_policy.setting: The place its stories name: graveyard, swamp, sea cliff, battlefield, celestial palace, desert storm. Weather and time of day heighten threat or majesty. Palette is dark and warm with one strong accent, consistent with the collection; no pastel, no flat even daylight.
user_policy.respect: Living religions (Hindu, Buddhist, Shinto, Abrahamic and folk deities still worshipped) are majestic and overwhelming rather than monstrous: cosmic scale, divine radiance from documented attributes, the elements they rule in motion. Malevolent beings are menacing. Literary beings follow their source text, never a film, game, anime or comic design.
user_policy.aniconic: If the research documents no bodily form at all, either depict the documented manifestation as an active, overwhelming force (the sky itself splitting, a storm swallowing the steppe) with the choice recorded in artistic_choices, or decline the entry with status tidak-digambar. A calm scene without agency fails.
user_policy.self_check: Before accepting an image the generator answers all of these with yes: the being dominates the frame; it still looks dangerous or majestic at 200 px; there is a moment, not a static pose; each visible effect points to a claim id; head, eye and limb counts match the claims; no text, watermark, border or borrowed design; it would not be rejected as ordinary person, ordinary animal, landscape only, or cute and calm. One no means regenerate, keep the rejected attempt as history, up to three attempts.
user_policy.style: Square premium painterly cinematic illustration in the house style of the existing artwork, more dramatic and higher contrast. No text, labels, logo, border or watermark.
user_policy.sources: Never copy designs from films, games, anime or comics (modern_depictions). Every design is original and sourced from the accepted research.
